gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, by Apple's own specs, the base-chip MacBook Air (M1, M2, and M3 with the lid open) drives only one external display, so on those Macs a two-screen extender such as the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro needs the maker's display software for its second screen, while one portable monitor fits within that one-display limit.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages and one cited top result. ViewSonic's dual-screen guide (cited) says extending across both screens of its own VG1457 doesn't work on macOS because of MST limits. It names no Apple chips and no rival product. bestusefultips.com (cited) says only 'Mac display limits depend on the exact Apple silicon generation and model' and 'Do not assume a laptop that can drive one external monitor can automatically drive two.' It gives no figures for any chip and names no models. Best Buy Canada's page (cited) showed no compatibility text in either part I read, just navigation, the intro and reviews. None of them gives Apple's one-display figures for base M1, M2 or M3, mentions the M3's lid-closed exception, or says which named extender needs a driver on which Mac.
decides: If the shopper has a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook Air and works with the lid open, the answer moves toward a single portable monitor or a single-screen extender. Those use the one external display Apple allows, with no driver. A two-screen extender will run its second screen only through the maker's display software. On Windows laptops with two USB-C ports that carry video, and on Pro, Max, M4 or M5 MacBooks, the finding doesn't count against two-screen extenders. Per Macworld, the Trio 3 Pro runs both screens on those Macs without the software.

findings.label: Apple MacBook Air (M1, 2020): external displays supported
findings.value: One external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz, plus the built-in display
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M1, 2020) - Tech Specs - Apple Support

findings.label: Apple MacBook Air (M2, 2022): external displays supported
findings.value: One external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support

findings.label: Apple MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024): external displays supported
findings.value: One external display up to 6K at 60 Hz with the lid open; a second, up to 5K at 60 Hz, only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: An extender clips to an open lid, so a base M3 Air gets one native added screen while you use it as a laptop.

findings.label: Which MacBooks run both screens without software
findings.value: Base M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' free software to run both screens. M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and M4/M5 Macs run both without it. Connection is by the two included USB-C cables; a power adapter on one Trio port passes up to 65 W to the laptop.
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Simon Jary writes that 'plain (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs plus the new MacBook Neo are limited to connecting just a single monitor.' He also writes that anything 'as or more powerful than a standard M1/M2/M3' runs both screens without the software. That doesn't match Apple's M3 MacBook Air spec (one external display with the lid open), so treat a base M3 like M1/M2 when the lid is open. Jary also says the screens can't reach full brightness on laptop power alone.

findings.label: Dual-screen extend on macOS
findings.value: Extend mode across both screens isn't available on macOS or mobile devices; only the lower display turns on when extending. Mirror mode and single-screen use work.
findings.source_title: Complete Guide to Dual-Screen Portable Monitors | ViewSonic
findings.note: This is a cited rival page. ViewSonic blames 'MST limitations over USB-C.' It covers only ViewSonic's own stacked dual-screen monitor and names no Apple chips.

findings.label: What the cited buying guide says about Mac compatibility
findings.value: Mac display limits 'depend on the exact Apple silicon generation and model.' No figures for any chip.
findings.source_title: Laptop Screen Extender Buying Guide: Compatibility & Setup
findings.note: This is a cited rival page. It does mention DisplayLink as a way around the limit of one native display. Read only to set the standout score.
